newsitem.title: USA: SPX closes Dutch auction, sets repurchase.
newsitem.headline: SPX closes Dutch auction, sets repurchase.

text.p: SPX Corp said Friday that 2,149,440 common shares have been accepted for purchase at a price of $56 per share under a Dutch auction which expired yesterday.
The Dutch auction, or self-tender offer, began on April 11, 1997. The company had offered to purchase 2.7 million SPX common shares at a price of not less than $48 nor greater than $56 per share.

At the end of first quarter 1997 and prior to the tender offer, SPX had about 14,877,014 common shares outstanding. Following the purchase of shares tendered in the Dutch auction, SPX said it will have about 12,727,574 common shares outstanding.
SPX also said its board of directors has authorized the company to acquire 750,000 shares through open market purchases.
The company said it will use funds from a new $400 million unsecured line of credit to purchase shares tendered in the Dutch auction.
SPX makes service tools and equipment for the motor vehicle industry.
